newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin discusses transfer of powers to PM.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin discusses transfer of powers to PM.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin met his chief of staff on Wednesday and discussed mechanisms for handing over power temporarily to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, the presidential press service said.

A statement issued after Yeltsin's talks with Anatoly Chubais, head of the Kremlin administration, gave no details but confirmed that the president had earmarked Chernomyrdin to deputise for him when he has a planned heart operation.

The statement said the discussion, in Moscow's Central Clinical Hospital where the 65-year-old Yeltsin is having tests, also covered ways to hand over to Chernomyrdin the "red button" which controls Russia's nuclear arsenal.

"Several questions on the mechanisms for transferring power, including control of the so-called 'nuclear button', to the chairman of the Russian government (prime minister) during the president's planned operation, were also discussed," it said.
Doctors are due to meet on September 25 or 26 to decide when Yeltsin should have a bypass operation to improve the flow of blood to his heart.
Chubais said in a newspaper interview published on Wednesday that he expected the president to hand over his duties to Chernomyrdin by decree for a maximum of two days.
